solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brother's reportedly drunk on gin

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on (after) another follows it

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for catching animals

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the next word is said aloud, not spelt

parts.note: drunk is slangily pissed, which sounds like the letters needed

explanation.surface: A monk is said to have got tipsy on gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' signals a sound-alike: the slang word for drunk is heard, not spelt, and 'on' sets it after the snare. 'Brother' here is a monk, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trappist is a monk of a strict Cistercian order, so a member is called Brother.

clue.text: Brilliant out-of-this-world plant died off with cold

indicators.note: off says the letter for died is taken away from the plant's name

parts.note: the triffid is the alien walking plant of John Wyndham's novel
D is the usual abbreviation for died in records
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A marvellous alien plant withered in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' drops the D from TRIFFID, leaving TRIFFI, and C is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Triffic is a jokey colloquial clipping of terrific, an informal word for excellent.

clue.text: We climb the odd bits of Tibet, for example

definitions.meaning: things that go upward, climbers or risers

definitions.text: the odd bits of Tibet, for example
definitions.meaning: the first, third and fifth letters of Tibet are T, b and t, each with a stroke rising above the line in typography

explanation.surface: Mountaineers boast of scaling the odd parts of Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography the tall strokes of letters like b, d and t rise above the x-height; climbers are also risers.

clue.text: Churned out repeats in D flat

indicators.note: churned means stirred violently, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A composer mechanically turns out repetitive pieces in the key of D flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means dull and uninspired, the same as flat in describing a performance.

clue.text: Means of detecting nitrogen in fly

indicators.note: in places the element symbol inside the word for flying

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone asks how nitrogen in a flying insect could be detected.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar uses echoed sound pulses to locate submarines and shoals, a detection system.

clue.text: Fancy man ultimately stopping harangue

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to harangue is to orate at length

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of man

explanation.surface: A dandy finally interrupts someone's tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means elaborately decorated, a synonym of ornate.

clue.text: Behind topless dowdy woman

indicators.note: topless in a down clue removes the top letter, the first

parts.note: a frump is a dowdy, unfashionably dressed woman

explanation.surface: A frumpy woman's backside is exposed with no top on.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the hindquarters or buttocks, informally one's behind.

clue.text: Burning desire

parts.note: read not as a passion but as the urge to set fire to things deliberately

explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of setting property alight, the act a pyromaniac's urge leads to.

clue.text: Lock lens cap after snapping

indicators.note: snapping means breaking apart, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A photographer locks the lens cap on after taking pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclasp is to hold fast in a clasp or embrace, to lock something in place.

clue.text: Individual parts stirred by these?

parts.note: an individual, a single person, is a man

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so the letters of parts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coy question about what gets a man's private parts excited.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a mantrap, slang for a predatory seductive woman, stirs a man's parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a woman who lures men, who would arouse an individual's private parts.

clue.text: Striking folk, for example, that may be arranged to back up action

definitions.text: that may be arranged to back up action

parts.note: incidental can mean falling upon or striking, as light hits a surface
folk is one kind of music

explanation.surface: Industrial strikers, for instance, can be organised to support a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking folk' suggests people on strike; it is two separate pieces, an adjective and a genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidental music is composed or arranged to accompany the action in a play or film.

clue.text: Net geek endlessly farts about with Windows

indicators.note: about means around and around, so these letters are jumbled
endlessly removes both ends of the word geek, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: A computer nerd keeps breaking wind while using Microsoft Windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves EE from GEEK; NET, EE and FARTS are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenestrate is a botanical and architectural term meaning having windows or window-like openings.

clue.text: Girl, last one on earth, found in seconds?

indicators.note: the question asks for the seconds, the second letter of each word

explanation.surface: A girl is the last person on earth, discovered within seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: More secret theft pinned on burglar — almost right

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is pinned on top of the second

parts.note: a steal is a theft, or a bargain

indicators.note: almost removes the last letter of the word

parts.note: a burglar is a thief

explanation.surface: A theft is blamed on a burglar who was nearly in the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive and covert, so stealthier is more secret in its manner.

clue.text: See you neck briefy with short funny guy

indicators.note: briefly (misprinted) cuts the final letter off the word

parts.note: neck means impudence, as does cheek

indicators.note: short means curtailed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a riot is a very funny person

explanation.surface: A goodbye to someone who has given a little lip to a short comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefy' is a printed typo for briefly. CHEEK minus K is CHEE; RIOT minus T is RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British farewell, a goodbye just like see you.

clue.text: Work that's noted to be light?

definitions.text: Work that's noted to be light?

parts.words: Work that's noted to be light?
parts.note: a work written in musical notes that is meant to be light entertainment

explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light opera, a musical work in a comic vein.

clue.text: Port/schnapps essentially passed to the left by idiot

indicators.note: by means beside, placing the two pieces side by side
in an across clue moving to the left means reading backwards
essentially picks the central letters, the essence of the word

parts.note: a twerp is a silly or foolish person

explanation.surface: A drink of port or schnapps is passed to the left by a fool at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes NA, the centre of SCHNAPPS; 'passed to the left' reverses it to AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major seaport in Belgium on the Scheldt.

clue.text: Drilling area protected by exhaust

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: eduction is the exhaust stroke or outlet in an engine

explanation.surface: A drilling site is shielded by exhaust fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Drilling is training by repetition, as in teaching; that is schooling.

clue.text: Top actors essentially get moved away from the audience

parts.note: up means at the top
the stage, the acting profession, is in essence actors collectively

explanation.surface: The leading actors basically get pushed to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like the definition (to outdo), but the blog takes the definition as the closing words, with 'get' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On a stage, upstage is towards the back, further from the audience.

clue.text: Bend with short stretching tool

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend, shortened to U

indicators.note: short removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: tensile means relating to tension or stretching

explanation.surface: A tool for bending, with a short extending arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement, especially a kitchen tool.

clue.text: Flapper associated with the proms?

parts.note: a winged creature that flaps around seaside promenades, not a 1920s girl at a concert or dance

explanation.definitionFit: Gulls flap their wings and haunt seafront walks, called proms in Britain.

clue.text: Child captivated by stories in which not a little is a lot?

definitions.text: in which not a little is a lot?

indicators.note: captivated means held captive, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: stories, untruths, are lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child is spellbound by tales in which little things are huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, so saying not a little means much.

clue.text: Nearly exact

definitions.meaning: ... as an old adverb for nearly, as in ... as near as dammit
... means exact or precise, as in an ... dozen

explanation.definitionFit: Even can mean precise, as an even pound, and in older use almost.

clue.text: Live or die without son

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to exit is to die, as in leaving the stage of life

explanation.surface: A stark choice: live, or die without a son.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, to live.

clue.text: Reserve I put forward to secure good entry on record?

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so this piece is enclosed
put forward means moved nearer the front of the word

parts.note: restraint is reserve, self-control

explanation.surface: A request to book ahead, putting oneself forward for a good entry in the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put forward' moves the I of RESTRAINT up to make REISTRANT, and 'to secure' places G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrant is one whose name is entered in an official register.

clue.text: Championship ponies bag a winning score

indicators.note: bag means to hold, so the words contain the letters

explanation.surface: Prize-winning ponies take a winning tally.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo an ippon is a full point, which wins the contest outright.

clue.text: Became half-cut, grabbing one's mistress

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing, so one piece is held inside another
half-cut keeps one half of the word, here its second half

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone got tipsy and grabbed a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' (slang for tipsy) leaves AME from BECAME; 'grabbing' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Amie is French for a female friend or girlfriend, a mistress in crossword usage.

clue.text: One with a liking for ink might also spit it out

definitions.text: One with a liking for ink

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tattoo enthusiast might also spit ink out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigmatophilist is attracted to tattoos and piercings, a lover of body ink.

clue.text: Do not start gossip that causes agitation

indicators.note: do not start means drop the opening letter of the word

parts.note: blather is foolish chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: An instruction not to begin gossip that stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a lather is to be in a state of agitation or fluster.

clue.text: Announced opening competitors

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is heard not spelt

parts.note: an entrance is an opening or way in

explanation.surface: The competitors were announced at the opening ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrants are those who enter a contest, its competitors.
